equation_summary: BDH attention: with K is Q (tied), scores = (RoPE(Q) @ RoPE(K)^T).tril(diagonal=-1) then scores @ V. diagonal=-1 makes it STRICT-PAST: position i reads only positions j<i, excluding the current token. There is NO softmax — it is a linear/additive reduction (positive after the ReLU sparsity nonlinearity F.relu(x_latent) upstream). Reading the strict-past scores is a READ-BEFORE-WRITE: the current token's own contribution is never in its read set. This is the canonical read-timing case; U2.A reads AFTER update and cannot be used unchanged.
state_shape: no explicit recurrent state; equivalent unnormalized linear-attention accumulation over strict-past positions (score matrix [T,T] lower-triangular excluding diagonal)
normalization: none (linear/additive, no softmax denominator; upstream F.relu provides positivity)

axis: read-timing axis (strict-past additive read-before-write K2 descriptor)
direction_justification: BDH is a strict-past additive read-before-write linear reduction (no softmax, no decay gate) that differs from the closed U2.A after-update contract by exactly the read-timing property, so it is a distinct closed descriptor / axis, not composition over U2.A.
open_questions: The full BDH block couples attention with the ReLU sparsity, encoder_v and decoder (neuron-like) projections; whether the strict-past additive law alone (without the surrounding sparsity/gating) is the reusable read-timing descriptor needs an independent reference
